transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Hi Mr. Park, thanks for coming back in to see me today. Please, have a seat.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Thank you.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I wanted to talk to you about your developmental screening. I looked through the charts and it seems there was some confusion with how the referral was handled.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Oh. I remember I missed one of the calls. I was in class.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Right, well, the system shows it as completed, but it actually wasn't. We had a bit of an issue with the tracking.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I thought I was supposed to get another call?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm sorry for any confusion here. We've been really understaffed lately and things just didn't quite get flagged correctly.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't really understand. Did I miss the appointment?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It's just that the paperwork didn't move forward. It's a system glitch, really.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is that bad? Like, is there something wrong with me?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. But we can fix it now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I was kind of worried because I didn't hear anything for three months. I thought maybe it was just how it works here.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Let me stop you there for a second because we need to move on to the solution. I have a lot of other patients waiting and I want to make sure we get this sorted quickly.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Oh. Sorry. I just thought maybe I did something wrong.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Not at all. It's just a clerical matter.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just feel a bit confused. I didn't know if I should have called you guys.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. Now, here is exactly how we are going to handle this. First, I have already called the screening clinic personally this morning. I have secured a priority appointment for you this coming Thursday at 10:00 AM.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Thursday? I have a lab.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: If you can move that lab, I can push this to Friday at 2:00 PM. Which is better?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Friday would be better.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Okay, I've noted Friday at 2:00 PM. Now, I am going to give you a printed slip with the clinic's direct phone number and the name of the coordinator, Sarah. You will take this slip with you. My office will also send a confirmation email to your student account by 5:00 PM today.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Thank you.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: To make sure this doesn't happen again, I've added a manual reminder to my own calendar to call you the day before the appointment to confirm you're all set. I've also flagged your file for "active follow-up" so that if any future referrals are declined once, the system will automatically alert me instead of marking it closed.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I didn't know there were alerts.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It's a new internal protocol I'm implementing for my patients. If you don't see that email by 5:00 PM, I want you to call my direct line immediately. Here is my card.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Okay. I'll do that.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Great. So, you have the appointment Friday at 2:00, you'll get the email today, and you have my number if the email doesn't arrive. Does that sound clear?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Perfect. Let's wrap this up so you can get back to your classes.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language ('I have a lot of other patients waiting', 'Let's wrap this up') and interrupts the patient's expression of worry ('Let me stop you there for a second').

E.justification: The resident never explicitly names the error, instead using platitudes and hedging such as 'some confusion with how the referral was handled' and 'a system glitch'.

A.justification: While the resident says 'I'm sorry for any confusion', responsibility is deflected to being 'understaffed' and a 'system glitch'.

R.justification: The resident uses generic validation ('I understand') but does not name specific emotions or engage with the patient's expressed worry.

T.justification: The plan includes specific next steps (Friday at 2:00 PM), timelines (email by 5:00 PM), a named patient role (call direct line if email doesn't arrive), and prevention (manual reminders and active follow-up flags).
